author: potuz
content: At 4 aggregators per committee I think we will see a lot of crying on client's discord servers

author: jtraglia
content: Currently, aggregator selection is uniform. I intend to make it balance-weighted, where validators with more stake are more likely to be an aggregator. While not always the case, validators with more stake are more likely to have better hardware/internet. Do you think this would help a bit?

author: potuz
content: I believe this is likely to not change much the situation until we see much more consolidation. But even in that case, the most likely source for a missed head vote today is peering with an aggregator. At 4 per subnet it'll be much harder to find them

author: jtraglia
content: Hmm because it takes too long to receive aggregates when you're not directly peered with an aggregator?

author: potuz
content: I am uncertain, I believe the topology is the biggest issue, cause when you're not directly peered it may take longer to reach the aggregator.

author: jtraglia
content:
> likely to not change much the situation until we see much more consolidation
So there are ~10k validators with 512 ETH or more. My napkin math tells me there's an 88% chance that at least one of four aggregators would have at least 512 ETH. If there were 16 aggregators, the likelihood would be 99.98% 😁

author: jtraglia
content: Also, a low-resource proposer would probably still be fine. They'd just need to include a single aggregate to propose. We wrote the following about this:

author: potuz
content: But that's not the statistic you want right? What you want is not too guarantee that there's one aggregate, you want a guarantee that every single attestation will reach an aggregate

author: jtraglia
content: Ah yeah, sorry I was spewing thoughts about a different concern. Where a validator doesn't have the resources to compute/send aggregates. Your point about peering is valid. I'm not sure what the appropriate balance there is.

author: tcoratger
content:
About the aggregators:

- Have we introduced a reward mechanism in the spec for them or do we just want them to do this for free (which was initially planned during our research)?

- For the required hardware material to become an aggregator, this is very light, as you can see in the leanVM benchmarks, everything is on CPU (no GPU at all) and our reference benchmarks are on Macbook M4, which should be a pretty normal machine for a validator I imagine.
